raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`--offload-during-compile` (#29862, on by default) layerwise-offloads the DiT for the torch.compile warmup, so max-autotune compiles each layer with only that layer resident. Residency is restored on the first non-warmup request. That is the real-path prewarm, which still runs during startup.

The restore does not bring back whole-graph compile. The warmup traces the offload hooks, and their `torch.compiler.disable` calls graph-break inside the block loop. Dynamo then skips the DiT frame, and it applies that skip to the code object for every later call: `ConvertFrameReturn` defaults to `FrameExecStrategy(SKIP, DEFAULT)` with `apply_to_code=True`. Removing the hooks changes nothing, so every request keeps running the per-block graphs the warmup left behind.

A toy reproduction is in the new test. It is a 3-block loop with a disabled pre-hook, compiled with `CompileCounter`. After the hooks are removed, serving compiles 0 frames. With this PR it compiles one frame with all 6 ops.

## Modifications

`DenoisingStage._offload_for_torch_compile_warmup` calls `torch._dynamo.reset()` right after `disable_offload()`. The next request compiles whole graphs from the autotune results the warmup already cached, so the compile peak that #29862 caps stays capped. That request is the real-path prewarm, at startup.

## Accuracy Tests

No numerical change beyond graph partitioning: the same kernels, fused across block boundaries instead of within each block.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

4xGB300, TP2, served, 1024x1024, `--enable-torch-compile true` with default flags (offload during compile on). Base: main 3831e7e09, the then-open GB300 fixes, #43601 and #43602. Each cell is the median of 5 requests after warmup. Two interleaved rounds (ABAB), each arm on a fresh server.

| case | before | this PR | change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen-Image-2.1, round 1 / 2 | 2.150 / 2.167 s | **1.672 / 1.556 s** | −22% / −28% |
| FLUX.1-dev, round 1 / 2 | 2.631 / 2.688 s | **2.531 / 2.561 s** | −4% / −5% |
| Z-Image-Turbo, round 1 / 2 | 0.945 / 0.912 s | 0.948 / 0.904 s | — |

Qwen-Image-2.1 comes close to the run with `--offload-during-compile false` (1.50 s). Z-Image does not move: with the flag off it serves in 0.57 s, so something else in its offloaded warmup still costs it.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests: `test_offload_during_compile.py`. It runs the real context manager around a compiled toy DiT. Warmup keeps the DiT offloaded. Serving compiles one whole graph (6 ops); without this PR it compiles none (`AssertionError: 0 != 1`). On GB300: 2 passed, against 1 failed / 1 passed on the base tree; with `test_layerwise_offload.py` on this branch rebased onto main 5730345: 199 passed.
- [ ] Update documentation: N/A.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

@@ -2068,6 +2068,10 @@ def _offload_for_torch_compile_warmup(self, batch: Req):
             module.disable_offload()
         # clear the list for avoid overhead during real request
         self._offloaded_dit_modules_for_compile.clear()
+        # The warmup traced the offload hooks, whose graph breaks inside the
+        # block loop make Dynamo skip the DiT frame for good. Forget it, so
+        # this request compiles whole graphs from the cached autotune results.
+        torch._dynamo.reset()
         yield
 
     def forward(

@@ -0,0 +1,83 @@
+"""Leaving the offload-during-compile warmup must not keep its graph breaks."""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+import torch.nn as nn
+from torch._dynamo.testing import CompileCounter
+
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.pipelines_core.stages.denoising import (
+    DenoisingStage,
+)
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+
+class _Block(nn.Module):
+    def forward(self, x):
+        return x * 2 + 1
+
+
+class _DiT(nn.Module):
+    """Blocks in a loop, each wrapped by an offload hook Dynamo cannot trace."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.blocks = nn.ModuleList(_Block() for _ in range(3))
+        self.hooks = [b.register_forward_pre_hook(_offload_hook) for b in self.blocks]
+
+    def disable_offload(self):
+        for hook in self.hooks:
+            hook.remove()
+
+    def forward(self, x):
+        for block in self.blocks:
+            x = block(x)
+        return x
+
+
+@torch.compiler.disable
+def _offload_hook(module, args):
+    return None
+
+
+class TestOffloadDuringCompile(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        torch._dynamo.reset()
+        self.dit = _DiT()
+        self.counter = CompileCounter()
+        self.dit.compile(backend=self.counter)
+        self.stage = SimpleNamespace(
+            _offloaded_dit_modules_for_compile=[self.dit],
+            _move_resident_components_for_warmup=lambda: [],
+        )
+
+    def _forward(self, *, is_warmup):
+        with DenoisingStage._offload_for_torch_compile_warmup(
+            self.stage, SimpleNamespace(is_warmup=is_warmup)
+        ):
+            self.dit(torch.ones(4))
+
+    def test_warmup_keeps_the_dit_offloaded(self):
+        self._forward(is_warmup=True)
+        self._forward(is_warmup=True)
+
+        self.assertEqual(self.stage._offloaded_dit_modules_for_compile, [self.dit])
+        self.assertTrue(all(b._forward_pre_hooks for b in self.dit.blocks))
+
+    def test_serving_compiles_the_whole_dit_after_the_warmup(self):
+        self._forward(is_warmup=True)
+        self.counter.frame_count = self.counter.op_count = 0
+
+        self._forward(is_warmup=False)
+        self._forward(is_warmup=False)
+
+        # One graph holding all three blocks; without the reset Dynamo keeps
+        # skipping the frame it gave up on during the warmup and compiles none.
+        self.assertEqual(self.counter.frame_count, 1)
+        self.assertEqual(self.counter.op_count, 6)
+        self.assertEqual(self.stage._offloaded_dit_modules_for_compile, [])
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
